title: AlphaSAGE: Structure-Aware Alpha Mining via GFlowNets for Robust Exploration
one_liner: Build trading formulas as structured objects and train a generator to spread probability across many high-quality formulas instead of collapsing onto one candidate.
lead: Automated alpha mining asks a system to search over many candidate trading formulas and return formulas that predict future returns. This is difficult because a useful score often appears only after a full formula has been completed, because the formula's tree structure matters to its behavior, and because practitioners need a set of weakly correlated formulas instead of one winner. AlphaSAGE addresses those three points together. It encodes each partial formula as a structured graph, gives the search process dense feedback at intermediate construction steps, and uses a flow-based generative objective that can keep probability mass on many good end states. The result is a search procedure that aims for quality and diversity at the same time.

problem.h2: Why alpha search breaks under sparse feedback
paras: A formulaic alpha is a program built from operators, variables, and constants that maps market data to a trading signal. The search space is huge because each decision about which operator to add, which input to use, and where to attach it changes the final behavior. A search system therefore needs guidance long before the full formula is finished.

Older reinforcement-learning approaches struggle because they often see the formula as a plain sequence and receive a useful reward only after the formula is complete. That makes learning unstable because early construction choices get almost no direct feedback. A second problem is portfolio construction: a desk does not want ten copies of the same idea. It wants multiple good formulas whose behaviors are different enough to combine well.

callout.html: Represent each candidate alpha by its structure and train a flow-based generator with dense rewards so the search keeps several good formula families alive because the final goal is a diverse portfolio, not one best formula.

steps.text: Treat the current formula as a typed graph so the model can tell which operator uses which input and which attachment sites remain open, because those relations determine the next legal construction step.
Score intermediate states using several criteria so the search gets guidance before the final formula is finished.
Use a generative flow policy to choose the next legal operator, variable, or attachment site.
Match the probability of reaching a formula to the reward of that formula so many strong endpoints can receive mass.
Select formulas that are predictive and not too correlated so the final basket is usable.

paras: The paper changes the search object from a plain left-to-right symbol stream to a structured formula state with typed relations. It also changes the learning target from expected return of one trajectory to flow matching over many rewarding endpoints, which matters because practical alpha mining needs breadth as well as quality.
object.object: the search mass over candidate alpha formulas

hidden.name: reward-weighted coverage of good formula families
paras: The important quantity is not only the score of the best discovered formula. It is how much search mass lands on different high-quality regions of the formula space. If all probability mass collapses onto one family, the system may miss other formulas that add portfolio value.

AlphaSAGE tries to increase reward-weighted coverage because a broader set of strong formulas gives a desk more options for diversification. The structure-aware encoder helps here by separating partial formulas that behave differently, and the dense reward helps because it keeps promising branches alive earlier in the construction process.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark areas where the search places mass on formulas that are both strong and clearly different.

reads.html: A good search process should keep finding several kinds of useful formulas because a portfolio gains value from variety.
The flow objective supports diverse reward-seeking samples by matching probability mass to terminal reward across many endpoints rather than only pushing toward one maximizer.

paras: A formula is naturally a tree or graph. Unary and binary operators attach to subexpressions, and the meaning of a partial formula depends on those relations. A structure-aware encoder therefore gives the policy a better state description because it can tell whether an operator is high in the tree, what operands it already uses, and which open slots remain. A sequential view loses much of that information.

The second key idea is the generative flow objective. Standard policy learning tends to concentrate on trajectories with the highest expected score, which is a poor match for alpha mining because multiple end states can be worth keeping. GFlowNets instead learn transition probabilities whose total flow toward an end state is proportional to its reward. That makes diversity easier because several high-reward terminal formulas can all receive probability mass.

Dense rewards matter for the same reason. Intermediate guidance reduces delayed-credit problems because the model gets feedback during formula construction rather than only at the end. Combining structured state encoding, dense rewards, and flow-based training makes exploration more stable and more useful for portfolio search.

stages.s: encode operator relations and open slots
score intermediate promise with dense reward
sample next construction action through flow policy
accumulate mass on many rewarding terminal formulas

math.words: For each complete formula, the total probability flow that reaches it should be proportional to its reward.
symbols: a construction trajectory that ends at formula x
the flow assigned to trajectory tau
the reward of formula x based on prediction quality and portfolio criteria
a normalizing constant that scales total flow

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose formula A has reward 6 and formula B has reward 3.
If the model is trained correctly, the total flow into A should be about twice the total flow into B.
That does not force all mass onto A because B still receives nonzero mass when its reward is still useful.
As a result, sampling from the trained policy can return both formulas, with A appearing more often because its reward is higher.

math.note: The exact training loss is more detailed, but this condition captures the point: reward sets how much mass a terminal formula should receive.

charts.title: Sequential search baseline
charts.note: A plain sequential search often rediscovers similar formulas because sparse feedback and collapse toward one mode reduce variety.

charts.title: AlphaSAGE
charts.note: The method improves all three because structure-aware states and flow-based learning support a broader set of strong terminal formulas.

items.b: Dense rewards can steer the search badly.
items.html: If an intermediate reward favors superficial formula patterns, the system may keep extending weak branches because the early score does not line up with final portfolio value.

items.b: Structure encoding depends on the operator grammar.
items.html: If the grammar omits useful operator types or relation labels, the encoder cannot represent important distinctions, so different formulas may look too similar.

items.b: Diversity without real quality is not enough.
items.html: A method can spread mass across many formulas yet still miss tradable signals if the reward does not reflect predictive value under realistic evaluation.

The reward should connect intermediate guidance to final predictive and diversification goals because the search policy can only preserve useful diversity when its score matches what the portfolio actually needs.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small symbolic formula grammar over synthetic price features, such as returns, moving averages, and volume changes. Define several hidden target rules so more than one formula family is predictive. Compare a sequential reinforcement-learning search against a flow-based search with a structured encoder.

Measure best formula quality, the number of distinct high-quality formula families recovered, and the average pairwise correlation among the top formulas. The demo should show that the flow-based method finds multiple strong families because its training objective keeps mass on several rewarding endpoints instead of collapsing onto one formula.
demo.closing: If coverage rises while the top formulas stay predictive, the method is solving the real alpha-mining problem rather than only finding one winner.
